title: From 1982 to 1987, Israel reintroduced 28 Asiatic wild asses to the Negev; after 10 more were released in 1992 and 1993, the herd reached about 250 | World News
text:
How the wild ass disappeared and came back
The Asiatic wild ass lived on the desert steppes of Mongolia, Russia, and the Arabian Peninsula. Today it survives in small isolated groups. In the Negev, it was gone by the 1920s, according to a 2013 article from Washington University in St. Louis. Because the animal could not be tamed, the local Bedouin hunted it for its meat. Alan Templeton, an evolutionary biologist, says water and World War I finished it off. In summer, nursing mothers must drink daily, but the displaced people settled near the few permanent sources of water and kept the asses at a distance. Without water, the mothers couldn’t raise their foals.
